candidates.proposed_human_problem: AI can make a difficult message smoother and more effective while making the recipient less certain whose feelings the words represent.
candidates.proposed_mechanism: Generative assistance lowers the cost of producing polished interpersonal signals; when authorship or delegation becomes salient, perceived authenticity can diverge from linguistic quality.
reach_notes: dating and message-writing are native human interests
recent 2026 survey provides a current adoption signal
clear expectation violation: better wording can weaken perceived authenticity
asset_notes: supports a relationship story without requiring technical literacy
candidates.observed_paradox: A message can become more tactful, fluent and 'correct' while feeling less like the person who supposedly sent it.
candidates.why_question: Why can AI make a relationship message better written but less authentically yours?
candidates.human_tension: linguistic correctness and conflict reduction vs authentic self-expression and costly personal signaling
candidates.controlling_question_seed: When does help expressing yourself become substitution for the part of expression that makes the message yours?
candidates.human_process_before_ai: People searched for words, tolerated awkwardness, revised, and personally bore the cost of revealing intent.
candidates.ai_changed_process: AI can draft, optimize tone, interpret subtext and supply replies before the sender performs that expressive work.
candidates.human_problem: The sender gains confidence and smoother communication, but the receiver may value the message partly because they believe the wording itself carries effort and intention.
candidates.human_stakes: trust, intimacy, conflict repair, dating signals and confidence in whose voice is present
candidates.ai_mechanism: LLM ghostwriting/editing reduces production effort and optimizes language; disclosure and degree of delegation alter authenticity judgments.
candidates.story_seed: Two people struggle over an important text. One uses AI to make every sentence perfect. The message succeeds—until the recipient learns how much of the vulnerable wording was delegated.
candidates.curiosity_gap: If the final words express what I really meant, why should it matter who drafted them?
candidates.audience_payoff: A practical mental model for separating editing assistance from delegation of the emotionally meaningful act itself.

candidates.proposed_human_problem: More autonomous agents make capability and authorization boundaries more consequential.
candidates.proposed_mechanism: Long-horizon tool use amplifies consequences when goals and permissions are not separately constrained.
asset_notes: already represented by stronger canonical topic
candidates.observed_paradox: The more independently an agent can act, the more valuable it is—and the more consequential its boundaries become.
candidates.why_question: Why does greater agent capability increase the need for explicit stopping and permission rules?
candidates.human_tension: delegation efficiency vs retained human control
candidates.controlling_question_seed: What should remain a human decision even when the agent can technically do it?
candidates.human_process_before_ai: People executed or explicitly approved consequential steps.
candidates.ai_changed_process: Agents can chain actions without a person at every intermediate step.
candidates.human_problem: Useful autonomy can cross from assistance into unauthorized action.
candidates.ai_mechanism: tool-enabled autonomous action plus permission/approval design
candidates.story_seed: An assistant receives all the keys because it is competent, then reaches a door competence alone never authorized it to open.
candidates.curiosity_gap: Why isn't technical ability enough to decide permission?
